title: all / all of; most / most of; no / none of etc.
subtitle: most people / most of the people / most of them
summary: Know when quantifiers like all, most, some and none need of (before the/my/these and it/us/them) and when they stand directly before a noun.

lesson.heading: all / some / most / no + noun
lesson.text: You can use **all, some, any, most, much, many, (a) little, (a) few, no** directly with a noun (some food, few books etc.). We do not say 'all of cars' or 'some of people'.

examples.text: **All** cars have wheels.
**Some** cars can go faster than others.
**Many** people drive too fast.
I go away **most** weekends.
I feel really tired. I've got **no** energy.
**Some** people learn more easily than others.

lesson.heading: some of / most of / none of + the / my / these ...
lesson.text: Before **the, this, that, these, those, my, your** etc. we use **of**: some of the people, some of those people (but not some of people); most of my time, most of the time (but not most of time).

examples.text: **Some of the** people I work with are very strange.
**None of this** money is mine.
Have you read **any of these** books?
I was ill yesterday. I spent **most of the** day in bed.

lesson.heading: all and half - of is optional
lesson.text: You don't need **of** after **all** or **half** when a noun follows.

examples.text: **All my** friends live near here. or **All of my** friends ...
**Half this** money is mine. or **Half of this** money ...

lesson.heading: In general or a specific group?

left.label: In general - no of
examples: **All** flowers are beautiful. (= all flowers in general)
**Most** problems have a solution. (= most problems in general)

right.label: A specific group - with of
examples: **All (of) these** flowers are beautiful. (= a specific group of flowers)
We were able to solve **most of the** problems we had. (= a specific group of problems)

lesson.heading: all of / some of / none of + it / us / you / them
lesson.text: Before **it, us, you, them** you always need **of**: all of us, half of it, none of them.

examples.text: *A:* Do you like this music? *B:* **Some of it**. Not all of it.
*A:* How many of these people do you know? *B:* **None of them**. / **A few of them**.
Do **any of you** want to come to a party tonight?
**All of us** were late.
I haven't finished the book yet. I've only read **half of it**.

lesson.heading: some / most / half alone
lesson.text: We also use **some, most, half** etc. alone, without a noun.

examples.text: **Some** cars have four doors and **some** have two.
A few of the shops were open, but **most** (of them) were closed.
Half this money is mine, and **half** (of it) is yours.

lesson.text: Look at the next word. the / this / my / them after the quantifier? Then you need of (most of the time, none of them). A noun on its own? No of (most people).

exercises.statement: There were problems at the airport and some of flights were cancelled.
exercises.explanation: ... some flights were cancelled. No of when the noun stands alone (some flights, not some of flights).

exercises.statement: Some of the films I've seen recently have been very violent.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Before the ... we need of: some of the films.

exercises.prompt: Do you want any ___ or can I throw them away?
exercises.explanation: Before these we use of: any of these magazines.

exercises.prompt: Kate has lived in London ___ her life.
exercises.explanation: Before her we need of: most of her life.
much of + my ...: much of my spare time.

exercises.prompt: Many ___ are caused by bad driving.
exercises.explanation: Accidents in general - no the, so no of: many accidents.

exercises.prompt: When Emily got married, she kept it a secret. She didn't tell any ___.
exercises.explanation: any of + her ...: any of her friends.

exercises.prompt: Not all ___ can fly. For example, the penguin can't fly.
exercises.explanation: Birds in general - all birds (no of).

exercises.prompt: Match the beginnings with the endings (all of / some of / none of + it / them / us).

pairs.left: 'How many of these books have you read?'
We all got wet in the rain because
pairs.right: none of us had an umbrella.

pairs.left: Some of this money is yours and
Many of my friends have travelled a lot, but
pairs.right: none of them has ever been to Africa.

pairs.left: I watched most of the film, but
He told us his life story, but
pairs.right: none of it was true. It was all invented.

exercises.prompt: I haven't finished the book yet. Put the words in order.
exercises.answer: I've only read half of it.
exercises.explanation: You need of before it / us / you / them: half of it (not half it).

exercises.prompt: Is the speaker talking about things in general or about a specific group?
categories: A specific group (all of / most of the ...)

items.text: All of these flowers are beautiful.
We were able to solve most of the problems we had.
Some of the people I work with are very strange.

exercises.prompt: Not all the tourists in the group were Spanish. ___ were French.
exercises.explanation: some of + them: Some of them were French.
